title: Building a simple compost heap cover
subtitle: A removable lid that keeps rain out and heat in without blocking airflow
excerpt: An uncovered compost heap gets waterlogged in UK winters and dries out in dry summers. Both conditions slow decomposition. A simple cover, a sheet of old carpet, a weighted tarpaulin, or a plywood lid fitted with a small ventilation gap, solves the moisture problem without sealing the heap. The build takes under an hour.
sourceNotes: RHS composting guidance. WRAP composting good practice sheets. Practical experience notes from gardening extension services.

content.text: A compost heap needs three things: moisture in the 40 to 60% range (like a wrung-out sponge), enough oxygen, and warmth. In a UK winter, an uncovered heap gets too much rain and drops below the active temperature range. It either goes slimy and anaerobic (too wet) or slow and dry (after a dry summer). A cover fixes this without blocking airflow. Most guides treat covering as optional, but in practice it speeds decomposition noticeably.

Old carpet or hessian sacking, the classic. Lay it face-down on the heap surface (wool or hessian side down, backing up). It keeps rain off, retains some heat, and can be peeled back for adding materials or turning. It breathes sufficiently to avoid anaerobic conditions. Synthetic carpet with a plastic backing is less good, it seals too well. Do not use carpet with foam or rubber backing.

Weighted tarpaulin, a 1.5 m × 1.5 m tarpaulin weighted at the edges with stones, bricks, or a rail of timber. Quick to remove for turning. In very wet weather, a 50 mm gap at the downwind side allows air circulation and prevents the heap going anaerobic.
For a fixed timber compost bin, a hinged plywood lid is the neatest solution and the easiest to use for daily additions. The build below suits a 1 m × 1 m bin, adjust dimensions to match your bin.
1 sheet 9 mm exterior plywood, 1,000 × 1,000 mm (or cut to bin size)
2 lengths 50 × 25 mm treated timber, each 1,000 mm, for stiffening battens across the underside
Wood screws 40 mm × 20 No., 25 mm × 10 No.
Exterior wood stain or paint for weatherproofing
Screw the two stiffening battens across the underside of the plywood panel at 250 mm from each edge. This prevents the lid bowing under rain and wind load.
Apply exterior wood stain to all faces. Allow to dry fully before fitting.
Fix the two hinges to the rear batten on the lid, then screw to the top rear edge of the bin. The lid should open smoothly and stay open at around 100°.
Drill three 25 mm ventilation holes through the lid at the front, 50 mm from the edge. Cover each hole with a short length of 25 mm mesh stapled over the hole to keep out flies.

A cover that completely seals the heap creates an anaerobic environment, the heap will smell of silage or sulphur. Any cover should allow some air exchange. If the heap develops an off-smell after fitting a cover, open a ventilation gap or remove it and replace with carpet.
